info.name: Notification Engine v2
info.description:
End-to-end flow for a project integrating with the notification engine.

**Run order:** run the whole collection top to bottom (Collection Runner or `newman run`). Folder 1 creates a fresh project and key and stores them in collection variables, so every run is isolated.

**Set before running:** `baseUrl` and `adminKey` (the engine's platform admin key). Everything else is filled in by the scripts.

**Real delivery:** with the engine in `aws` mode set `recipientEmail` to an address verified in SES (sandbox) and `waitMs` to about 4000. `SENT` means the provider accepted the message.

Never commit real keys: `adminKey` and `apiKey` are secrets and are empty in the committed environments.

item.name: 0 Health
item.description: Public, no API key. Use it to check the engine is reachable.

request.description: Returns `{"status":"UP"}` when the engine and its database are healthy.

item.name: 1 Admin onboarding
item.description: Done once per project by the **platform admin** (uses `adminKey`). The project key is returned ONCE and stored hashed.

request.description: Creates the tenant. `code` must be unique and lowercase. Optional: sesConfigSet, smsSenderId, smsEntityId, rateLimitPerMin, dailyQuota.
The raw key is returned only in this response. The engine stores a SHA-256 hash. Give each service/environment its own key with the narrowest scopes.

exec: pm.test("key shown once, starts with ntf_", function () { pm.expect(b.key).to.match(/^ntf_/); });

request.description: The raw key cannot be retrieved after creation (only a hash is stored). Use this to see which keys exist, their scopes and when they were last used. If a key was lost, issue a new one and revoke the old one.

exec: pm.test("shows prefix, label and scopes but never the raw key", function () { pm.expect(keys.length).to.be.above(0); pm.expect(keys[0].prefix).to.be.a("string"); pm.expect(JSON.stringify(keys)).to.not.include(pm.collectionVariables.get("apiKey")); });
pm.test("contains the demo project", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().map(function (p) { return p.code; })).to.include(pm.collectionVariables.get("projectCode")); });

item.name: 2 Templates
item.description: Wording lives in the engine, not in the calling backend. Placeholders such as `{{name}}` are required at send time. Run as the project (`apiKey`, scope TEMPLATES).

body.raw:
{ "code": "approval-requested", "channel": "EMAIL", "locale": "en", "subject": "Approval needed for weighment #{{id}}", "bodyHtml": "

Hi {{name}}, weighment #{{id}} needs approval.

", "bodyText": "Hi {{name}}, weighment #{{id}} needs approval." }

request.description: For India, set `dltTemplateId` to the DLT-approved content template id; the text must match it exactly.

item.name: Create a new version of the EMAIL template

request.description: Creating an existing code/channel/locale adds a version. New notifications use the latest active version; each notification pins the version it was accepted with.

body.raw:
{ "code": "approval-requested", "channel": "EMAIL", "subject": "Approval needed for weighment #{{id}}", "bodyHtml": "

Hi {{name}}, weighment #{{id}} needs approval.

", "bodyText": "Hi {{name}}, weighment #{{id}} needs approval." }

item.name: 3 Send notifications
item.description: `POST /notifications` returns **202**; delivery is asynchronous. A stable `idempotencyKey` per business event makes retries safe.

request.description: Typical backend trigger. Contact data and variables are never returned by the API.

exec: pm.test("202 with one notification per channel", function () { pm.expect(body.notifications.length).to.be.above(0); });

request.description: Same idempotencyKey returns the original notification. Safe to retry after a timeout.

exec: pm.test("same notification id, nothing resent", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().notifications[0].id).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get("notificationId")); });
pm.test("one row per channel", function () { pm.expect(n.length).to.eql(2); });
pm.test("in-app is delivered immediately", function () { pm.expect(n.filter(function (x) { return x.channel === "IN_APP"; })[0].status).to.eql("DELIVERED"); });

request.description: With the engine in `aws` mode this needs SNS SMS access (and DLT registration for India).
`channels` omitted: the engine uses its configured default for the category (SUCCESS -> IN_APP).

item.name: 4 Status and history
item.description: Poll for the result. `SENT` = accepted by the provider, not delivered to the inbox. These requests wait `waitMs` first to give the worker time.

exec: var end = Date.now() + wait; while (Date.now() < end) {}
pm.test("sent by a worker", function () { pm.expect(n.status).to.eql("SENT"); pm.expect(n.attempts).to.eql(1); });

item.name: Retry a notification that is not retryable

request.description: Only FAILED notifications with retryable=true can be retried (retries exhausted). Permanent failures and sent notifications return 409.

exec: pm.test("error body has a correlationId and no stack trace", function () { var b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b.correlationId).to.be.a("string"); pm.expect(JSON.stringify(b)).to.not.include("Exception"); });

item.name: 5 OTP
item.description: One-time codes have their own controls: only a salted hash is stored, expiry, attempt limits, resend cooldown, single use. The code is **never returned by the API**; it is delivered to the recipient. To test the success path, paste the received code into the `otpCode` variable and run *Verify OTP (correct code)*.

exec: pm.test("returns a challenge, never the code", function () { pm.expect(b.challengeId).to.be.a("string"); pm.expect(JSON.stringify(b)).to.not.match(/\d{6}/); });

pm.test("error body has a correlationId and no stack trace", function () { var b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b.correlationId).to.be.a("string"); pm.expect(JSON.stringify(b)).to.not.include("Exception"); });

pm.test("error body has a correlationId and no stack trace", function () { var b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b.correlationId).to.be.a("string"); pm.expect(JSON.stringify(b)).to.not.include("Exception"); });

request.description: Skipped automatically when `otpCode` is empty (the code is only delivered to the recipient).

exec: if (!code) { pm.test.skip("set otpCode to the code you received to test the success path"); }

item.name: 6 Preferences
item.description: Consent per user, channel and category. OTP, VERIFICATION and SYSTEM are mandatory; MARKETING needs explicit consent.

exec: pm.test("cancelled, kept for audit", function () { var n = pm.response.json().notifications[0]; pm.expect(n.status).to.eql("CANCELLED"); pm.expect(n.lastErrorCode).to.eql("PREFERENCE_OPT_OUT"); });

pm.test("error body has a correlationId and no stack trace", function () { var b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b.correlationId).to.be.a("string"); pm.expect(JSON.stringify(b)).to.not.include("Exception"); });

item.name: 7 Inbox and devices
item.description: In-app notifications for one end user. `recipientRef` is the calling project's own user id (the project is trusted because it holds the key).

exec: pm.test("has unread in-app items", function () { pm.expect(p.total).to.be.above(0); });
